 On November 17, 1999, the panel heard the repeat claim of XXXXXX XXXXXXX XXXXXXX XXXXXXX XXXXXXXXX to be a Convention refugee. At the conclusion of the hearing, the panel rende red an oral positive decision. These are the written reasons which have been edited for syntax and grammar, with added references to the documentary evidence where appropriate. XXXXXX XXXXXXX XXXXXXX XXXXXXX XXXXXXXXX, you are a 29-year-old citizen of Guatemala who claims Convention refugee status because of your membership in a particular social group. You allege a fear of persecution in Guatemala at the hands of the powerful XXXXXX family who controls the Q'eqchi (Ketchi Kekchi) people in Alta Verapaz. You also fear the army because you became, through your work, an advocate of the indigenous people of the area. You allege that you confronted this po werful family at a public meeting, in the Municipality of Panzos, and, as a result, attempted to report the XXXXXX family activities to the authorities. This met with little results from the authorities, but caused members of that family to pursue you even though you made several attempts to relocate with your job. At the same time, you allege that the military also pursued you. You concluded that this was at the instructions of the XXXXXX family. The panel recognises that most of this story was contained in your first hearing of December 11, 1997. However, the panel has t oday considered not only the evidence of the witness before us but also the copiou s documentation which confirms that this powerful family are intertwined in their activity with the military. Therefore, given all the documentary ev idence which is recent, the panel does consider that it has new evidence before it not available at the prior hearing. The documentation before the panel not only corroborates the past atrocities related by you, but more importantly as refugee law is forward looking, it directs the panel to look at the current and on-going situation in Guatemala.

 2 The panel refers to the following exhibits: C-2, C-4, C-5, C-6, C-7 and C-8. The panel will not quote from these documents today. Counsel has referred the panel to the pertinent sections to consider and you have heard what these pertinent sections were. The panel also considered the new document from the Rural Socio-Educational Development Directorate dated September 13, 1999 in C-4, page 138, which gives corroborative evidence of your status as an advocate for the council of Q'eqchi indigenous people. Considering your prof ile and the attention you drew from the XXXXXX family and the military, and given the knowledge provided by your witness, Mr. XXXXXXXXXX, who served with the Un ited Nations Verification Mission in Guatemala (Minagua), from 1996 to 1999, the pane l finds that there is more than a mere possibility that if you were to return to Guatemala you would be persecuted for your membership in a particular social group, that is, activists who have publicly challenged a powerful land owner family such as XXXXXXXXXXXX, who are connected to the military. The panel recognises as stated in the 1998 DOS
1 report, that Congress has approved a number of key reforms envisioned by the Peace Accord. These reforms recognise the multi-ethnic pluric cultural and multi-lingual nature of the country and permit a civilian Minister of Defence as well as redefine the role of the military. However, these reforms will not go into eff ect until approved by a citizens' referendum planned for in 1999. The panel has no evidence before it that confirms that this has taken place. The panel recognises Mr. XXXXXXXXXX, the witness before us, as an expert witness, given his credentials in Exhibit C- 3, and detailed during his testimony. The panel accepts his statement corroborated by other evidence that land reform was not in the agenda for the Peace Accords. It is not now on the agenda for peace reforms nor will

After careful consideration of all of th e evidence, the Refugee Division determines that XXXXXX XXXXXXX XXXXXXX XX XXXXX XXXXXXXXX is a Convention refugee. "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
